summary: Trump talks up momentum on Iran, three-way Ukraine talks open in Abu Dhabi, Israel's new Knesset sits, China's surplus tops $1 trillion, and COP31 begins.

question.text: Trump says the Iran war is "effectively over" and that there is momentum toward a deal, while Iran says there are no real talks. Without inside access, what evidence in the coming weeks would tell you which description is closer to the truth?

read.title: Qatar PM to meet Trump: What's the latest on US-Iran negotiations?
read.summary: A clear explainer of where US-Iran talks stand: Iran's seven conditions, the US position, and why Qatar is the go-between.

topics.heading: Trump sees "positive momentum" on Iran after meeting Qatar's prime minister
topics.summary: After White House talks with Qatar's prime minister, the main go-between, Trump said the war was "effectively over" militarily and new strikes were unlikely for now.[^1][^3] Iran's top security official told the US to stop talking about "imaginary talks" and accept Tehran's seven conditions.[^3]

lead.title: Trump claims war 'effectively over', Iran presses on conditions

alsoReported.title: Qatar PM to meet Trump: What's the latest on US-Iran negotiations?

article: On Monday, President Trump met Qatar's prime minister, Sheikh Mohammed bin Abdulrahman Al Thani, at the White House. Qatar carries messages between Washington and Tehran. Afterwards Trump wrote that they had "an excellent conversation" about Iran, said there was "positive momentum" toward ending the conflict, and called the war "effectively over" in military terms, while keeping new strikes as an option.[^1] He wrote that Gulf states "would prefer the status quo" and told Reuters the US is still "ready to go anytime".[^3]

The meeting followed a week of mixed signals. Iran sent a new proposal through Qatar, but says it can be discussed only after the US meets seven demands, including lifting sanctions, releasing frozen funds, cutting US forces in the region, recognising an Iran-Oman shipping route through Hormuz, and ending the war "on all fronts", including Israel's strikes on Lebanon.[^2] Secretary of State Marco Rubio called those demands "outrageous and ridiculous" and said there was no breakthrough close.[^2]

Iran's reply was cool. Mohsen Rezaei, head of its Supreme National Security Council, told Washington to stop "manufacturing fake news about imaginary talks" and to accept the seven conditions.[^3] The Financial Times reported that Israel's Prime Minister Netanyahu has urged Trump to restart the war, while Arab leaders urge talks; that report comes from unnamed sources.[^3] The Qatari prime minister was due to meet European and Saudi ministers on the sidelines of the G7 in Paris on Tuesday.[^1]

My read: both sides now describe the pause as something they can live with, but neither has moved on the core issues, Iran's nuclear material and control of Hormuz. A real test would be whether direct talks resume, or the US naval blockade is eased, in the coming weeks.
topics.differences: Trump says there is "positive momentum" and a "good chance" of a deal.[^1][^3] Rubio said a day earlier that talks had not progressed.[^2] Iran's Rezaei says there are no real talks until the US accepts Iran's conditions.[^3]

topics.heading: US, Russia and Ukraine begin their first three-way talks since February in Abu Dhabi
topics.summary: Delegations from the US, Russia and Ukraine opened two days of talks in Abu Dhabi focused on security guarantees, the first such meeting since February.[^5][^6] Europe is present on the sidelines, and both sides still disagree sharply on territory.[^7][^8]

lead.title: U.S., Russia and Ukraine begin talks in Abu Dhabi aimed at ending war in Ukraine

alsoReported.title: Russia and Ukraine security-focused talks start in Abu Dhabi
Russia, Ukraine, and the U.S. to hold peace talks in Abu Dhabi on November 10

article: Talks between the United States, Russia and Ukraine began in Abu Dhabi on Tuesday and are planned to run two days.[^5] They are the first three-way meeting since February; diplomacy largely stalled after the US went to war with Iran.[^5] US envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner lead the American side, and a US official said they expect to cover security guarantees, meaning promises about who would defend Ukraine against a future attack.[^6]

The delegations are senior. Russia's is led by presidential aide Vladimir Medinsky with two deputy foreign ministers and the head of military intelligence; Ukraine's is led by foreign intelligence chief Rustem Umerov.[^7] European officials from the EU, NATO, Germany, France and the UK are in Abu Dhabi for separate meetings but are not at the main table, which the Kremlin insists is three-way.[^7][^8]

The gaps are wide. Russia demands that Ukraine leave four regions, including areas Russia has not captured, drop its NATO bid and accept limits on its army.[^5] President Zelenskyy rejects giving up territory and says Ukraine needs firm guarantees and a ceasefire first.[^5] Trump says he believes the war will "end soon"; a senior Ukrainian lawmaker told ABC he expects little beyond possible prisoner swaps.[^8] Overnight, Ukraine's air force said Russia launched 162 drones and a missile.[^8]

At the G7 meeting in Paris, European ministers pressed Rubio to make any deal fair to Ukraine, and Germany's foreign minister said Europe "must have a place at the table".[^4] Canada announced new sanctions on 38 entities and 24 people.[^4] My read: a limited result, such as a prisoner exchange or an energy truce, is more plausible this week than a breakthrough on borders.
topics.differences: Kushner calls the talks a first step that could "build momentum".[^5] Moscow says the talks are strictly three-way, while France says Europe will be represented.[^8][^4] Ukrainian MP Oleksandr Merezhko has "absolutely no hopes" beyond prisoner swaps.[^8]

topics.heading: Israel's new Knesset is sworn in as Eisenkot searches for 61 seats
topics.summary: Israel's new 120-seat parliament was due to be sworn in on Tuesday, with neither Netanyahu's bloc nor Gadi Eisenkot's holding a majority.[^9] Eisenkot has the first chance to form a government, and his opposition plans to name Matan Kahana as speaker.[^9]

lead.title: New Israel parliament to be sworn in as Eisenkot seeks government

article: Israel's 26th Knesset, elected last month, was due to be sworn in on Tuesday, with President Isaac Herzog speaking at the opening session.[^9] The result left neither main camp with the 61 votes needed for a government. Herzog gave opposition leader Gadi Eisenkot, a former army chief, the first mandate on Sunday, starting a 28-day clock that can be extended by 14 days.[^9]

Eisenkot's core bloc has 48 seats, according to AFP. He could reach a majority with the 19 Arab-Israeli lawmakers, most likely by having them vote for a government without joining it.[^9] But Avigdor Lieberman, a key ally, says he will not let Eisenkot rely on Arab parties and has suggested a deal with the two ultra-Orthodox parties, which hold 13 seats and have backed Netanyahu until now.[^9]

In the meantime the opposition plans to use its numbers in parliament. It will nominate Matan Kahana, a former senior military figure, as speaker and Lieberman to chair the foreign affairs and defence committee.[^9] One stated priority is a state commission of inquiry into the security failures that allowed the October 7, 2023 Hamas attack, which Netanyahu has resisted.[^9]

Why it matters beyond Israel: the next government will decide how Israel handles the stalled next phase of the Gaza ceasefire and the war with Iran. AFP notes Eisenkot has largely supported past war decisions but promises to act against extremist settlers in the West Bank.[^9] My read: the coalition maths may take most of the 28 days, and a second election cannot be ruled out.

topics.heading: China's trade surplus passes $1 trillion for a second year as exports jump 35%
topics.summary: China's customs data show October exports up 35.2% from a year ago and a surplus of $1.04 trillion for January to October, led by chips and cars.[^10] Economists say weak demand at home keeps China leaning on sales abroad, ahead of Trump-Xi talks next week.[^10]

lead.title: China's trade surplus surpasses $1 trillion for a 2nd straight year, as exports surge 35%

article: China's customs agency said on Tuesday that exports in October were 35.2% higher than a year earlier, and imports rose 41.6%.[^10] That pushed the trade surplus, the amount by which exports exceed imports, to $1.04 trillion for the first ten months of 2026, the second year in a row above $1 trillion. China is on track to beat last year's record of about $1.2 trillion.[^10]

The details show what the world is buying. Chinese semiconductor exports rose 137% in value in October and car exports 37.6%, as the global AI building boom pulls in electronics.[^10] Exports to the US rose 32.9% and to the EU 24.3%. Imports grew partly because crude oil shipments from the Persian Gulf recovered.[^10]

Economists see a problem underneath the strength. Alicia García-Herrero of Natixis says overcapacity, high savings and weak spending at home keep China exporting, and calls this "not sustainable".[^10] Small exporters describe fierce price wars. An economist at Moody's Analytics expects exports to stay strong this year, but names an AI slowdown and new EU trade limits as risks.[^10]

Trade is expected to top the agenda when Trump and Xi Jinping meet next week at the APEC summit in Shenzhen; a trade truce was recently extended to January.[^10] My read: a surplus this big makes other countries more likely to add tariffs, which is one of the main pressures to watch in 2027.

topics.heading: COP31 opens in Antalya with its host saying 1.5C will be overshot
topics.summary: The UN climate summit opened in Turkey after a year of deadly extremes, and its president said it is now clear the world will pass 1.5C of warming.[^11] Poorer countries want clarity on money; the US is not taking part.[^11][^12]

lead.title: COP31 climate summit begins after disastrous year of extreme weather

alsoReported.title: COP31 enters 2nd day with focus on energy, transport

article: COP31, the yearly UN climate summit, opened in Antalya, Turkey, on Monday and runs to November 20.[^11] About 68,500 people have registered. Turkey hosts the meeting, while Australia leads the formal negotiations; the United States is absent, having pulled out of the climate talks.[^11]

The mood is sober. Turkey's environment minister Murat Kurum, the COP president, said this is the first COP where it is "clear beyond a reasonable doubt" that the world will overshoot the 1.5C limit set in Paris in 2015.[^11] UN climate chief Simon Stiell called the climate crisis "a global health crisis" and framed the choice as "electric or shock", pointing to how the Iran war has driven up fuel and fertiliser prices.[^11]

Kurum wants this summit to turn past promises into action rather than set new targets, with an "Action Agenda" on methane and resilient cities and a goal to raise electricity's share of energy use from 21% to 35% by 2035.[^11] The second day focused on energy security, power grids and transport, with about 370 sessions.[^12]

The main fight is money. Developing countries want rich ones to say how they will pay for adaptation; Meena Raman of Third World Network said the poorest countries "shouldn't have to borrow their way through it".[^11] The African Group's agenda proposals are contested by the EU and Canada, an adviser to African negotiators said.[^11] Leaders speak on Nov 11-12.

topics.heading: Scientists project fossil CO2 emissions will dip in 2026, partly due to the Iran war
topics.summary: The Global Carbon Budget projects fossil CO2 emissions will fall 0.4% in 2026, helped by solar and wind and by the oil shock from the Iran war.[^13][^14] Its authors warn a fall caused by a crisis is not a lasting solution.[^13]

alsoReported.title: Iran war disruption expected to curb global fossil fuel emissions, scientists say

article: An international team of scientists, the Global Carbon Project, published its yearly estimate on Tuesday. It projects that carbon dioxide from burning fossil fuels will fall 0.4% in 2026, to 38.2 billion tonnes.[^13] Emissions from oil are expected to drop 1.9%, likely a short-term response to the energy shock from the Iran war, while gas falls 0.3% and coal rises 0.6%.[^13][^14]

Countries move in different directions. The study projects falls of 1.5% in the EU, 1.3% in the US and 0.9% in China, but a 4.4% rise in India.[^13] A linked paper in Nature Climate Change finds that solar, wind and electric vehicles are covering most new energy demand, and that 59 countries cut emissions below 2019 levels in 2025 while their economies grew.[^13]

The total picture is less good. When fires and forest loss are included, total CO2 emissions still rise, to 43.3 billion tonnes, because of peat fires in Southeast Asia.[^13] CO2 in the air reaches about 427.7 parts per million, 54% above pre-industrial levels, and the remaining budget for 1.5C is about 150 billion tonnes, less than four years at today's rate.[^13]

The lead author, Pierre Friedlingstein, said a drop "driven partly by geopolitical shocks is not a sustainable climate solution".[^13] Glen Peters of CICERO added that one year's fall is not a peak unless it comes from lasting change.[^13] The numbers arrive as COP31 negotiators meet in Turkey.
